nom: Pure Body Naturals Bentonite Clay Powder

segments.oily: One reviewer says the mask absorbs oil and leaves his face feeling less oily and less congested, alongside a reduction in mild breakouts.
segments.sensitive: Reviewers caution this product especially against use on sensitive skin, citing a burning sensation and visible reaction marks after just one application; one reviewer specifically warns she would not recommend it for sensitive skin or those who have reacted to clay masks before.
segments.normal: One reviewer without sensitive skin or known allergies reports a painful burning sensation and visible redness along her jawline after a single use, which she suspects may be linked to having used retinol five to seven days earlier.
segments.mature: One reviewer in her late 30s reports that after two months of twice-weekly use, the fine lines around her eyes and forehead had noticeably lessened and her pores looked less noticeable.

concerns.aging: One reviewer reports that after two months of consistent twice-weekly use, the fine lines around her eyes and forehead had noticeably lessened and her complexion looked more even.
concerns.dehydration: Several reviewers note the mask is very drying and stress the need to moisturize heavily afterward; one says it dries and tightens skin faster than other bentonite clay masks she has used.
concerns.redness: Redness is a common and often expected reaction: several reviewers see mild redness after rinsing that fades within about an hour, in line with the product's own label warning; a few dissenting reports describe more severe reactions with burning, red welts or visible marks that did not fade quickly, one of whom recommends against use on sensitive skin.
concerns.barrier: A couple of reviewers with eczema say the clay itself did not irritate their eczema-prone skin (one noting the only sting came from mixing in apple cider vinegar) and one reports it helped calm eczema on her hands almost immediately; several other reviewers, without stated skin conditions, report burning and welts severe enough that they would not recommend it for reactive skin.
concerns.blemishes: Several reviewers with acne-prone or breakout-prone skin report visibly clearer skin and fewer blackheads within days to a few weeks of regular use, including one managing hormonal breakouts during perimenopause who uses it three times a week mixed with apple cider vinegar.
concerns.oiliness: One reviewer says the mask absorbs oil and leaves his face feeling noticeably less oily and less congested.

extraits.texte: I bought this because I use the Healing Aztec Clay once or twice a week and it’s quite costly at $16 per container. I saw this listed at half the price and I saw reviews that said it was the same thing. No, no, no!! This burned my face—BURNED—and I do not mean the hot, pulsating feeling that the real Aztec Clay causes. This was burning. Like hot water on my face. Even my lips burned and the mixture was not even on my lips! My eyes were irritated and burned, too! I now have red, welts on my cheeks and forehead! Don’t buy this! Just splurge a little bit more and buy the real thing. I promise you, it’s worth spending the money than to have burned and irritated cheeks, lips, and eyes.

extraits.titre: Beware: Had a Burning Reaction After Use
extraits.texte: I wish I had just bought my original Aztec clay mask. I decided to try something different because it was a bit cheaper and I needed something quickly, but that turned out to be a mistake. I applied this product for about 10 minutes and rinsed it off, and it caused a burning sensation and left my face with visible reaction marks. I’ve never experienced anything like this before with skincare products. I would NOT recommend this, especially if you have sensitive skin or have used clay masks in the past. I’ll be going back to my original Aztec clay mask.

I am unsure of this product. It is kind of hard to mix but I knew it would be. My daughter and I both used it and hers seemed normal. She liked the way it felt after. Mine however was very painful. It didn’t even dry all the way before I HAD to wash it off. After washing my face was still burning and I had full face irritation. Some parts worse than others. The patterns on the jaw line are odd. I went down to just below the jaw line but you can see that I have an odd line of redness. I do not have sensitive skin and no known allergies. There is no itch or real swelling. Just a burning feeling. Only thing I can think of is that I used retinol 5-7 days ago.

extraits.texte: Wow! I wish I would have known about this sooner…. I am a 40 year-old female going through perimenopause and to say that my hormonal breakouts are unbelievably awful is an understatement!!! I get pores that get clogged with spacious hyperplasia!! and to make it more understandable, let’s just say it’s like having a poor that is a nonstop leaky clear faucet coming out of your face. I love that this is all natural from volcanic ash, but I must say read the directions!!!! do not use a metal spoon or a metal bowl because it will have an electric charge reaction…. I read if you have acne prone skin like myself do this mask about three times a week I plan on doing a bath as well. My photos are about five minutes in and you start to feel like a crusty elephant, but a good one! I can’t wait to see the before and after photos after a few uses but so far so great! I recommend mixing it with apple cider vinegar instead of water if you have acne prone skin like myself and let’s just face it. Apple cider vinegar is good for your body inside and out. If you’re just doing a face mask, you only need to use 1 tablespoon of the powder and 1 tablespoon of apple cider vinegar for only 15 minutes and rinse off with warm water, it also helped the eczema on my hands almost immediately!!!
